definitions.explanation: A male employee of a company who receives a regular salary. The term represents the typical Japanese corporate employee, especially in business contexts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{普通|ふつう}→普通：01502_futsuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧サラリーマン⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: My father is an ordinary office worker.

examples.japanese: サラリーマン⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{悪|わる}くない→悪い：00908_warui⟧。
examples.english: Life as a salaryman isn't bad.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧サラリーマン⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦いっぱい→いっぱい：01793_ippai⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The area in front of the station is full of office workers.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: English 'salary' + 'man' (wasei-eigo/Japanese-made English)

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE: The term サラリーマン became iconic during Japan's economic growth period (1960s-1980s), representing the dedicated corporate worker who prioritizes company loyalty.

GENDER NOTE: サラリーマン traditionally refers to male workers. The female equivalent is ⟦OL→OL：07717_ooeru⟧ (オーエル, 'office lady'), though this term is increasingly seen as outdated. More gender-neutral terms like ⟦{会社員|かいしゃいん}→会社員：03018_kaishain⟧ (company employee) are now preferred.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・サラリーマン⟦{金太郎|きんたろう}→金太郎：noentry⟧ (a popular manga character)
・⟦{脱|だつ}サラ→脱サラ：29183_datsusara⟧ (leaving corporate employment to start one's own business)
・サラリーマン⟦{川柳|せんりゅう}→川柳：09660_senryuu⟧ (humorous poems about office life)
